title: Consumer reports 0.6.1 did not fix docs/log.md clobbering
description: A lore consumer reports log.md still truncating on 0.6.1. NOT reproduced, and deliberately not closed as works-for-me. Evidence against, gathered 2026-09-13 against the PUBLISHED 0.6.1 binary (global install verified byte-identical to the registry tarball, shim removed): (1) worst-case unreachability -- a purpose-built fixture with a 15-entry log across 16 commits, history then replaced by an orphan commit carrying the identical tree so 100 percent of logged commits were unreachable; 15 of 15 carried forward plus the new commit, zero lost; (2) idempotency -- two further syncs byte-identical; (3) CRLF -- log.md rewritten with CRLF, zero lost, so the trailing-CR strip is live in the published bytes. opum-agent independently measured +1/-0 on its own repo and on a clean registry install. Remaining hypotheses, in order: the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 (different npm prefix, vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update); a DIFFERENT failure mode being misattributed to LCLI-474; or a shape no fixture has covered. UNCLOSED PLATFORM GAP: only the darwin-arm64 binary was exercised. win32-x64 and win32-arm64 are separately compiled artifacts and CRLF is precisely where they diverge -- the CRLF test simulated CRLF bytes on macOS, which is not the same as the Windows binary on a core.autocrlf=true checkout. Ask the consumer's PLATFORM first; it is one question and it splits the search space.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The consumer platform is known, and if Windows the win32 binary is exercised on a core.autocrlf=true checkout rather than simulated CRLF on macOS
Which lore binary the consumer actually ran is established from their filesystem -- resolved path plus version -- not from npm view
Either a reproducing fixture exists and the defect is fixed, or the report is resolved as not-0.6.1 or as a distinct failure mode with that mode named
If a distinct failure mode, it gets its own task rather than being folded into LCLI-474s record
